paper.title_en: Non-Gaussian Halo Bias from Tensor-Induced Density Perturbations
paper.abstract_en: Primordial gravitational waves induce matter density perturbations at second order. Because this sourcing is quadratic in tensor modes, the induced density field is intrinsically non-Gaussian even for Gaussian tensor modes. Here we compute the scale-dependent halo-bias correction generated by this tensor-induced density bispectrum for a Gaussian-bump tensor spectrum with a peak tensor-to-scalar ratio $r_*=0.002$. At low wavenumbers, both the induced density power spectrum and the bispectrum form factor approach finite, nonzero constants. Their ratio consequently produces a large-scale plateau in the bias correction defined relative to the tensor-induced density power spectrum. Over the sampled scales, the fractional Eulerian correction reaches a maximum of $1.85\times10^{-10}$. When evaluated relative to the total matter power spectrum, the fractional correction remains below $4.0\times10^{-25}$ across the sampled scales and halo populations. Its scale dependence differs from that of the standard local, equilateral, and enfolded primordial non-Gaussianity templates.
